1.w: And Job continued to lift up his discourse, and he said,

2.w: “Who will make me as [in] months past, as the days [when] God was keeping me?

3.w: In His lamp shining upon my head, by His light I walked [through] darkness,

4.w: as I was in the days of my harvest time, when the counsel of God was upon my tent,

5.w: when yet Shaddai [was] with me, my children around me,

6.w: with the washing of my steps with cream, and the rock poured out for me streams of oil!

7.w: [Or] in my going out [to] the gate upon the town, in the square I established my seat;

8.w: the young men saw me and hid themselves, and old men arose [and] stood;

9.w: the princes refrained from words, and they put a hand on their mouth;

10.w: the voice of the nobles was hidden, and their tongue stuck to their palate.

11.w: For the ear heard and declared me blessed, and the eye saw and testified for me,

12.w: because I rescued the poor crying out, and the fatherless, and no one was helping him.

13.w: The blessing of the one perishing came upon me, and the heart of the widow I caused to sing.

14.w: I clothed myself with righteousness, and it clothed me; like a robe and a turban [was] my justice.

15.w: I was eyes to the blind, and I [was] feet to the lame.

16.w: I [was] a father to the poor, and the case I did not know, I searched it out.

17.w: And I broke the fangs of the unjust, and I cast away the prey from his teeth.

18.w: So I said, ‘In my nest I will die, I will multiply [my] days as the sand.

19.w: My root is open to the waters, and the dew lodges on my branch.

20.w: My glory [is] fresh within me, and my bow in my hand is renewed.’

21.w: They listened to me and waited, and they kept silent for my counsel.

22.w: After my word, they did not speak again, and my speech dripped upon them.

23.w: And they waited for me as for the rain, and their mouth they opened wide, as for the spring rain.

24.w: I smiled at them, [and] they could not believe [it], and the light of my face they did not let fall.

25.w: I chose their path and sat [as] chief, and I dwelt as a king with [his] band, like one who comforts the mourners.
